prompt: A clothing retailer's inventory has grown 35% in a year while sales fell 5%. Markdowns doubled. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Lighter markdowns have likely made the stock harder to sell.
Buying has probably stayed high as demand fell, piling up stock.
options.feedback: Right. Inventory grew 35% while sales fell 5%, so buying didn't track demand, and markdowns doubled to clear it. I'd compare purchase orders with sales by category.

options.text: The buyers ordered the wrong styles, and that explains the whole problem.
options.feedback: This states one cause as the whole explanation before any data has tested it.

options.text: Demand has probably surged and the stores can't keep up.

explanation: The data shows inventory up 35% while sales fell 5%, and markdowns doubled. Likely cause: buying stayed high as demand fell. To test it, compare purchase orders with sales by category. If orders fell in line with sales, look at the product mix instead.
